newsitem.title: USA: Moler sworn in as U.S. deputy energy secretary.
newsitem.headline: Moler sworn in as U.S. deputy energy secretary.

text.p: Elizabeth Moler was sworn in Monday as deputy energy secretary, an Energy Department spokeswoman said.
Moler goes to the No. 2 job at the department from the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission, where she has been chairwoman since February 1993 and a commissioner since 1988.
In her nine years at the FERC, the commission completed the restructuring of the wholesale natural gas business and adopted major rules opening the wholesale power market to competition.
Before joining the commission, she was senior counsel to the Senate Energy Natural Resources Committee.
Moler was in line to be nominated as Energy Secretary last December, but was dropped at the last minute in favour of Federico Pena.
Industry officials have speculated that she took the No. 2 job with the promise that Pena might leave within a year.
